name: Street Custom 'Rosary' Bead Garrote
description:
A garrote wire concealed within a string of decorative beads worn as a bracelet or necklace. The beads are machined from tungsten carbide and threaded on a 1mm monofilament wire with breaking strength of 400 kilograms. When deployed — unclasped and drawn taut between two hands — the wire cuts through unprotected tissue in seconds, and the tungsten beads provide grip points that prevent the wire from slipping through the operator's hands.

Rosary garrotes are Shelf craft — assembled by hand from industrial monofilament and machined beads, then disguised as costume jewelry. They are worn openly, passed through security checkpoints without comment, and carried in environments where no other weapon could enter. The Rosary exploits the most fundamental assumption of weapons screening: jewelry is not dangerous.

The weapon requires close physical contact and significant upper-body strength to deploy effectively, limiting its use to ambush or grapple scenarios. But its concealability is unmatched — a Rosary looks like a piece of inexpensive jewelry, weighs almost nothing, and shows up on X-ray as exactly what it appears to be: a string of metal beads. Only someone who recognizes the specific bead material and wire type would identify it as a weapon, and that requires expertise that most security personnel do not possess.
legality: Unregulated — classified as jewelry (weaponized use constitutes assault)
specifications:
wire material: 1mm monofilament, 400 kg breaking strength
bead material: Tungsten carbide, 8mm diameter
total length: 60cm deployed
weight: 85g
form factor: Bracelet or necklace
tactical_use: Close-quarters assassination from ambush or grapple position. The Rosary requires the operator to be behind or above the target with both hands free. Once deployed, the monofilament cuts through neck tissue faster than the target can respond. The weapon leaves a distinctive wound that experienced forensic examiners can identify.
cultural_context: The Rosary garrote occupies a strange cultural space in the Shelf — it is both a weapon and a genuine piece of community jewelry. Many Shelf residents wear monofilament bead strings without any intention of using them as weapons, simply because they are inexpensive and attractive. This makes identifying actual weapon-carriers impossible. The ambiguity is the point.
known_users: Shelf residents (both as jewelry and weapon)
Anyone who expects to be thoroughly searched
story_hooks: A corporate bodyguard was killed with a Rosary garrote in a crowd — the attacker deployed the wire, made the cut, and vanished into the press of bodies in under three seconds. Security footage shows dozens of people wearing similar bead jewelry. The killer is in the footage. So are forty innocent people wearing the same accessory.

A jeweler in the Shelf has been arrested for manufacturing Rosary garrotes — but the arrest is cover for something else. The jeweler's client list includes names from the upper tiers, people who shouldn't know the Shelf exists, let alone be buying weapons from it.

physical_description.visual_profile: An elegant string of decorative beads indistinguishable from costume jewelry at casual glance. The tungsten carbide spheres catch light with a subtle metallic sheen. When worn, it drapes naturally as a bracelet or necklace. The deception is its defining characteristic—it appears fragile and ornamental.
physical_description.dimensions: 60cm deployed length; individual beads 8mm diameter; 1mm monofilament wire gauge
physical_description.weight_description: Featherlight—85g total, barely noticeable when worn. The minimal weight enhances its jewelry disguise and allows extended wear without fatigue.
physical_description.primary_material: Tungsten carbide beads threaded on 1mm monofilament wire (likely polyethylene or similar synthetic fiber rated to 400kg breaking strength)
physical_description.finish: Tungsten carbide beads possess a satin-matte metallic finish with subtle gray-silver tone. The monofilament is nearly invisible, creating the visual illusion of floating beads
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray with faint metallic highlights. Some street variants use mixed bead finishes or anodized accents to enhance the costume jewelry aesthetic
physical_description.grip_texture: The beads themselves are smooth and cool to the touch. When deployed as a garrote, the tungsten carbide spheres provide knurled anchor points for bare fingers or gloved hands—grip is secure despite the weapon's delicate appearance
distinctive_features: Perfect spherical tungsten carbide beads with microscopic precision machining
Nearly invisible monofilament creates 'floating bead' visual effect
Minimal clasp mechanism—typically a simple magnetic or friction lock disguised as jewelry hardware
No manufacturer branding visible (street craft production)
Subtle wear marks on beads from hand contact during concealment
Wire may show microscopic fraying at clasp points from repeated deployment
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: None—street custom assembly by hand leaves no serial numbers or identifying stamps. This anonymity is intentional
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine cosmetic condition maintained deliberately; any visible damage compromises its disguise. Combat-used variants may show minor bead surface scratches or slight wire discoloration but are otherwise indistinguishable from new

image_prompt: Close-up product photography of a tungsten carbide bead garrote disguised as delicate costume jewelry, draped across a dark matte surface. The beads are rendered in satin metallic gray, catching dramatic side-lighting that emphasizes their perfect spherical geometry and subtle surface reflections. The nearly-invisible monofilament creates an optical illusion of floating beads suspended by light alone. A gloved hand (chrome-augmented fingers visible) gently lifts one end of the bracelet, revealing the weapon's elegant deception. Extreme shallow depth-of-field isolates the beads in sharp focus against a blurred cyberpunk neon backdrop—rain-wet pavement, distant holographic storefronts. The image conveys lethal beauty: ordinary-looking jewelry transformed into precision assassination tool. Tungsten carbide detail shots show manufacturing perfection.
